unit_division_review.json.scope: Finite nonzero a,b; long double native precision; FE_TONEAREST. No library source edits.

identities.ties: fl(b/a)==1 iff a==b; fl(b/a)==-1 iff a==-b. Strict/opposite comparisons therefore also agree.

proof.notation: Let p be binary significand precision and x,y positive representable finite values. The representable neighbors of1 are1-2^-p and1+2^(1-p). Their nearest-rounding midpoints are1-2^(-p-1) and1+2^-p.
proof.above_one: If y>x, the next representable gap above x divided by x is at least1/(2^p-1)>2^-p for normal x; subnormal x has an even larger relative gap. Thus y/x>1+2^-p, beyond the upper rounding midpoint. Its rounded quotient is strictly>1 or+Inf.
proof.below_one: If 0<y<x, the predecessor gap divided by x is at least2^-p. Equality can occur for a normal power of2; other normal or subnormal relative gaps are larger. Thus y/x<=1-2^-p<1-2^(-p-1), below the lower midpoint. Its rounded quotient is strictly<1, including possible underflow0.
proof.signs: Opposite-sign division is nonpositive, so +1 comparison is trivial; same-sign division reduces to positive magnitudes. Correct nearest rounding is sign symmetric, giving the -1 comparison.
proof.consequence: Only exact equal magnitudes can yield a rounded quotient of±1. No nextafter fallback is needed at unit boundaries. This proves agreement with the stored floating boundary itself regardless of how its intersection rounded.

safety_requirements: Keep finite input validation in checked mode when removing the combined quotient/result guard; result=Inf alone does not prove finite inputs. SKIP already assumes finite inputs.
For finite inputs and abs(a)>=1, b/a cannot overflow. For abs(a)<1, retain existing quotient-overflow detection, even when point selection uses direct unit comparisons.
Keep NaN dot-product cancellation recovery. Infinite dot results remain allowed.
Do not extend the comparison shortcut to boundary0: a=LDmax,b=denorm_min gives rounded quotient+0 although b>0.
Other rounding modes and manually reduced x87 precision-control are outside this proof.

dual_bound_review.json.scope: Independent code inspection of cached previous/positive boundaries and mutable add_hull hint. No main edits or duplicate full tests.

reasoning.early_returns: Both early returns precede hull.insert. intersection writes only local candidate/previous copies, so live p values and cached boundaries remain unchanged.
reasoning.tracked_previous: The previous boundary depends on previous/positive coefficients. Suppression excludes inserted slopes inside the tracked inclusive range and interior deletions promote refresh, so the pair remains unchanged.
reasoning.tracked_positive_with_after: When adjacent.after exists, its coefficient pair with positive remains unchanged under suppression; positive.p remains valid.
reasoning.tracked_positive_without_after: Suppressed insertion beyond positive may change its p while retaining positive. The unconditional end-of-add update on !refresh && !after copies the new live p even if changed=false after the candidate is subsequently erased.
reasoning.removals: Every actual predecessor/successor removal is preceded by mark_removed. Removing positive or any tracked endpoint promotes refresh=true and actual removal makes changed=true, so the end !refresh branch cannot dereference an erased positive pointer.
reasoning.allocation_or_throw: Allocation failure is handled by outer add catch+clear. Floating intersection/update operations do not throw C++ exceptions here; there is no partial update path skipping the end copy other than the pre-insert returns.
reasoning.cache_false: All new cached field access is under if constexpr(cache_points), and Hint& is used only from nonconst add-owned state.
reasoning.other_tags: refresh can be false only in tag3 tracking; small1/2 and tag0 paths keep full refresh. Copy recomputes both bounds; move/swap copy matching caches; clear resets hints.

narrow_radius_review.json.scope: Only added tag4 radius shortcut. No code edits or duplicate full oracle run.

proof.endpoints: negative.previous==nullptr means negative.line is first. positive.line->p==+Inf implies last under strict monotone boundary invariant. positive.previous is therefore previous last.
proof.range: All finite boundary p values lie between first.p and prevlast.p. R=max(abs(first.p),abs(prevlast.p)) encloses this interval. c>R selects last and c<-R selects first.
proof.ties: The shortcut uses abs(c)>R strictly; equality and all interior ratios fall back to original lower_bound. Stored rounded boundaries, not ideal exact intersections, define the same selection convention.
proof.state: Tag4 is computed only after ordinary >=3-line, non-shared initialization. It cannot overwrite small1/2 or a genuine shared3 due preceding return or contradictory previous conditions. add_hull only suppresses refresh for small==3, so tag4 hull changes always refresh its points and radius. Rejected additions that leave hull unchanged need no refresh. Copy refresh recomputes; move/swap preserve matching hull addresses; clear zeroes hint.
proof.math_protection: The shortcut only changes line selection. Nonfinite ratio or result still goes to existing checked_result/recovery. For +Inf ratio it returns last, -Inf first; NaN fails shortcut and falls back to lower_bound before existing invalid-input protection. Finite c with true overflow result remains allowed as before.
proof.floating_zero: R>=0 and abs(±0)>R is false, so signed-zero and underflowed ratio retain original tree selection.

symmetric_invariant_review.json.scope: Tag5 symmetric center shortcut as described by parent; implementation source not yet inspected. No edits or tests.
preconditions: Existing tag3 with previous and adjacent.after both present.
Stored boundaries satisfy positive.p == -previous.p and R=positive.p>0.
Refresh suppression for tag5 uses the same inclusive slope interval as tag3 and mark_removed retains its inclusive deletion check.
reasoning: Each line boundary depends only on its coefficient pair with the immediate successor. previous.p depends on (previous,positive); positive.p on (positive,after).
Suppressed insertions occur strictly outside the inclusive interval from adjacent.before (or slope-order infinity) through after. They cannot insert between previous/positive or positive/after.

Removing/replacing a node in either pair or an endpoint falls inside the inclusive tracked interval and promotes refresh. Therefore suppressed additions leave both coefficient pairs and the two stored p values unchanged.
The argument mirrors for MINIMIZE slope order because the interval checks mirror the comparator order.
With symmetric finite R>0, abs(c)<R lies strictly in (previous.p,positive.p). abs(c)==R falls back to lower_bound to preserve negative-boundary tie selection.
Outside the central interval, previous/after cached points are selected only using their existing live before/after boundary tests; otherwise tree search preserves existing behavior.
If after is absent, an insertion beyond positive can change positive.p without deleting positive, so retaining the after-present requirement is the correct conservative condition.
checks_for_implementation: Tag5 participates in tag3-style refresh suppression only if the same inclusive interval/deletion checks are retained.
Positive cached.p stores R only after tag5 is selected; other tags must ignore stale R.
Outside-range helper must preserve strict before.p<c and c<=after.p comparisons and fall back on equality where required.
Existing quotient/result safety remains after point selection.

review.scope: Public floating max_ld/min_ld only use Line value selection under Clang+SKIP. Optional remains v31 reference/evaluation wrapper; integer proof and argmax selectors use reference; GCC and checked branches retain original selection and min negation wrapper.
review.unit_tag: Only Clang+SKIP, cached binary IEC559 MinHull of size2 with stored boundary exactly±1 gets tag4/5. Generic reference selector treats those tags as ordinary two-line hulls.
review.unit_math: The separately proved unit-boundary comparison identity preserves strict lower_bound tie choice. negative_a switches b>p*a to b<p*a exactly when dividing by negative a. boundary p*a is a or-a, so no multiplication overflow.
review.safety: All callers enter unit body only with nonzero a,b. SKIP retains documented finite-input precondition. abs(a)<1 always performs existing quotient finite guard in cold helper, preserving ratio-overflow exception even when chosen point value is finite. abs(a)>=1 proves ratio finite. NaN dot cancellation recovery and legitimate infinite results remain intact. Checked/GCC paths do not use this shortcut.
review.state_lifetime: No new owned storage, pointer, allocation or persistent member. Tag4/5 never participates in small3 refresh suppression. A changed two-line hull recomputes caches/tag; rejected candidates do not change hull. Copy recomputes; move/swap keep caches matched with transferred multiset nodes; clear resets. Early-return and deletion behavior of add_hull are unchanged.
review.fallback: Deduced Hint type makes discarded cached accesses valid when cache_points=false. Both checked/SKIP instrumented false configurations run all3 oracles under standard arithmetic fallback.
review.rounding_contract: Root API documents default rounding/native precision and unspecified zero sign. Unit proof is limited to correctly rounded binary division; radix2+is_iec559 gates encode representation assumptions. Finite nonzero direct-min values preserve nearest rounding, while zero signs are not guaranteed.
